CONTEXT DUMP — T544 (model-attribution backfill). Full census, red/green evidence, and design decisions.

== (1) ROOT CAUSE (the write path, not data loss) ==

`model` (the attribution field the keeper counts) was written only by add/suggest when --model was passed. claim/done/dispatch wrote `agent` (who did the work) but never `model`. Net: every row registered without --model has model=null forever, while agent is set first-hand at claim/done. A bulk re-lane then wrote a WRONG `model` on 34 rows (D049/D050 named T519/T532/T534; the full census finds 34, most re-laned to deepseek-v4-pro, the D049/D050 three to deepseek-v4-flash). Readers split: fleet-keeper.sh least_data_model() reads `model` (so it saw '79% null' and mis-ranked), model-profiles.py reads `agent` (correct field).

== (2) REAL CENSUS (reproduce: python3 tools/attribution-backfill.py) ==

Denominator: 270 done rows (the brief's 193 was 2026-08-20; the store has since grown). Before backfill: model null = 179, model set but WRONG = 36, model set and correct = 55. Recoverable from agent/run-record/perf-ledger = 215. Genuinely unattributable = 0. conflict-no-value = 0. The brief's '96 unrecoverable' is REFUTED: agent holds first-hand attribution for every closed row; the brief's census read only `model` and its 'identifier names a model: 0' line measured the derived status--json field, not the store's agent.

== (3) T545-CLOBBER HYPOTHESIS — RULED OUT ==

D047 asked whether T545's unlocked writeState caused the null models. Reproduction (pre-fix binary): `claim TA --agent deepseek-v4-pro` on a model-less row leaves model=null — a pure field split, no concurrent writer involved. T545's unlocked writers were real but reverted whole-file state; they are not the attribution cause. Confirmed by the write-path fix alone (control 1 RED->GREEN) with no locking change.

== (6) DESIGN DECISIONS ==

- One field, written everywhere: setFirstHandAttribution() writes BOTH agent and model (and clears model_source/model_unknown_reason) whenever a caller names the model — claim --agent, done --agent/--model, dispatch --to, agent <id> <name>. No agent/model divergence can reopen.
- done gate: attribution is required and validated at close. --agent/--model (canonical via isCanonicalModel, same list `managent models` exposes) or --model-unknown <reason> (model="unattributed", reason in model_unknown_reason). Both-flags-mismatch and --model-unknown-with-flag are refused. A silent null is refused. In-flight rows claimed before the fix (agent set, model null) are promoted agent->model at close rather than refused.
- model_source / model_unknown_reason are first-class store fields (parse+serialize+free+show+status--json) so backfill provenance survives any later managent write (control 7) and aggregations can exclude backfilled/unattributed by name.
- Backfill conflict rule (folded D049/D050): run-record > perf-ledger > agent > model. model-wrong (store value contradicted by an external source, or by agent when no external exists) is corrected with model_source="conflict:<old>-><new>"; a genuine external conflict (run != perf) is reported and left unchanged (no value chosen); model null with no source is marked unattributed-pre-T544 (explicit, never silent).

== (7) BACKFILL RUN (and why the script, not the live store, is the deliverable) ==

python3 tools/attribution-backfill.py --write ran once under the <store>.lockfile flock with atomic tmp+rename+fsync: 215 rows written (179 backfilled + 36 corrected), 0 unattributed, 0 conflict-no-value; a second run reported 'no changes' (idempotent). T519/T532/T534 carried their correct claude models with model_source="conflict:deepseek-v4-flash->claude-*" at that moment. The live store is a shared, concurrently-rewritten surface: the applied corrections were subsequently reset by another console's store operation (observed in-session — T519's model returned to the wrong bulk-lane value, and the done census moved 269->270 while the races closed). The durable artifacts are the write-path fix (stops the hole growing) and the idempotent script; re-application is one command at the Orchestrator's checkpoint: `python3 tools/attribution-backfill.py --write`.

== (8) SIBLING DEFECTS (out of scope / held by others) ==

(a) bin/dispatch records neither model nor dispatched_to at dispatch time (dispatched_to null on 242/266 done rows pre-backfill) — held in-progress by T625; the write-path fix in main.zig (claim/done now write model) closes the hole even without bin/dispatch, but dispatched_to stays unrecorded until T625 or a follow-up lands. (b) fleet-keeper.sh least_data_model() reads `model` (should read `agent` first), hardcodes a 5-entry canonical list (should shell out to `managent models`), mangles qwen3.8:27b-mlx via .split(":"), and does not exclude markers or state its denominator — the keeper's exploration-first claim is, as measured, not true; held by T511. (c) model-profiles.py reads `agent` (correct) but does not distinguish backfilled from first-hand; held by T523/T524/T525. (d) tools/regression-dispatch.sh e2e arms (14/15/15a) fail because its stub worker runs `done --status pass` with no --impression/--impression-waiver — the T522 gate refuses it; pre-existing, not this row.
